items.title: Ordered configuration space
items.statement: For n≥0 and a space X, F_n(X)={(x_1,…,x_n)∈X^n:x_i≠x_j for i≠j}, with the subspace topology; a based configuration q is fixed only when F_n(X) is nonempty. F_0(X) is a point.

references.title: Juan González-Meneses, Basic results on braid groups, §§1.1–1.3 and 2.1, printed pp. 3–6, 11–13
Fadell–Neuwirth, Configuration Spaces, §II Theorems 1 and 3, printed pp. 111–114

items.proof_strategy: Use the finite product topology and the inherited subspace topology. The point labels are part of the data; deleting the collision diagonals precedes all group actions.

items.title: Free coordinate-permutation action
items.statement: S_n acts continuously on F_n(X) by permutation of coordinates, and this action is free for every X.

references.title: Juan González-Meneses, Basic results on braid groups, §§1.1–1.3 and 2.1, printed pp. 3–6, 11–13

items.proof_strategy: For σ define (σ·x)_j=x_{σ^{-1}(j)} so it is a left action. Coordinate projections and the product universal property prove continuity. If σ fixes a tuple, pairwise distinct coordinates force σ(j)=j for every j; the n=0,1 cases are immediate.

items.title: Unordered configuration space
items.statement: C_n(X)=F_n(X)/S_n with the quotient topology; the basepoint for q∈F_n(X) is its orbit [q]. Elements are unordered n-element subsets with this quotient topology.

references.title: Juan González-Meneses, Basic results on braid groups, §§1.1–1.3 and 2.1, printed pp. 3–6, 11–13
Fadell–Neuwirth, Configuration Spaces, §II Theorems 1 and 3, printed pp. 111–114

items.proof_strategy: Define the orbit quotient of the preceding free action. In a Hausdorff space the set description is literal; retain the quotient topology rather than asserting an unproved hyperspace topology.

items.title: Conjugating loop classes by a path is an isomorphism of fundamental groups
items.statement: For a path c from x_0 to x_1 and the first-then-second concatenation, φ_c([α])=[(c̄*α)*c] is a well-defined group isomorphism π₁(X,x_0)→π₁(X,x_1) whose two-sided inverse is φ_c̄; in particular π₁ at two points of one path component are isomorphic.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, section 1.1, printed p. 28, Proposition 1.5

items.proof_strategy: Concatenation respects path homotopy rel endpoints (step 1.1), reparametrisation does not change the class (step 1.2) and a path cancels its reversal (step 1.3). Inserting and deleting the cancelling pairs makes φ_c well defined, multiplicative and inverted by φ_c̄; a bijective homomorphism is an isomorphism.

items.title: Closed-disk and interior-disk configuration equivalence
items.statement: For D²={z∈C:|z|≤1}, the inclusions F_n(int D²)→F_n(D²) and C_n(int D²)→C_n(D²) are homotopy equivalences, compatible with the quotient and with interior base configurations.

references.title: Juan González-Meneses, Basic results on braid groups, §§1.1–1.3 and 2.1, printed pp. 3–6, 11–13
Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, §0 homotopy equivalence, printed p. 3

items.proof_strategy: The radial map r(z)=z/2 on every point sends the closed disk into its interior. On either configuration space H_t(z_1,…,z_n)=((1−t/2)z_1,…,(1−t/2)z_n) is collision-free, S_n-equivariant, and joins identity to inclusion∘r or r∘inclusion. It descends to C_n and fixes no claim of pointwise basepoint preservation: for π₁ use the explicit radial basepoint path; one may choose the standard q near the center and state the induced basepoint-change isomorphism.

items.title: Evenly covered coordinate neighborhoods
items.statement: If X is Hausdorff and q∈F_n(X), then the quotient F_n(X)→C_n(X) evenly covers an open neighborhood of [q] with n! sheets; n=0 is the identity on a point.

references.title: Juan González-Meneses, Basic results on braid groups, §§1.1–1.3 and 2.1, printed pp. 3–6, 11–13
Fadell–Neuwirth, Configuration Spaces, §II Theorems 1 and 3, printed pp. 111–114

items.proof_strategy: Choose finitely many pairwise disjoint open U_j containing q_j. Let V be the image of ∏U_j intersected with F_n(X). Its inverse image is the disjoint union of σ(∏U_j), σ∈S_n. The quotient is open since saturation of any open set under a finite group of homeomorphisms is open. Each restriction to a sheet is a homeomorphism onto V, giving the required evenly covered neighborhood.

items.title: Regular configuration covering
items.statement: For a nonempty connected Hausdorff d-manifold M, possibly with boundary, of dimension d≥2, F_n(M)→C_n(M) is a connected regular n!-sheeted cover, with deck group S_n acting by coordinate permutations.

references.title: Juan González-Meneses, Basic results on braid groups, §§1.1–1.3 and 2.1, printed pp. 3–6, 11–13
Fadell–Neuwirth, Configuration Spaces, §II Theorems 1 and 3, printed pp. 111–114

items.proof_strategy: Apply the preceding sheets. A connected manifold M is path connected; small local detours in R^d or a half-space chart show removal of finitely many points leaves the needed paths, including near boundary points. Choose a fresh intermediate configuration disjoint from both endpoint configurations, move labelled points one at a time to it and then to the target, so F_n(M) is path connected. The n! coordinate maps are deck transformations. A deck map of a connected cover is determined by its value at one point, so these exhaust the deck group and act transitively on each fiber. Treat n=0 and n=1 separately.

items.title: The closed disk is a manifold with boundary
items.statement: D²={z∈C:|z|≤1} is a nonempty connected Hausdorff second countable topological 2-manifold with boundary, with explicit interior translation charts and boundary charts φ_q(w)=i(q-w)/(q+w) at every |q|=1. Added locally in this batch to supply the manifold-with-boundary hypothesis of the regular-covering theorem at M=D².

references.title: Ioan Marcut, Manifolds (2017 lecture notes), sections 14.5 and 15.1
Nigel Hitchin, Differentiable Manifolds, section 2.2

items.proof_strategy: Prove convexity by the triangle inequality to get connectedness, heredity of Hausdorffness and second countability from R^2, translation charts at interior points, and the Möbius boundary chart φ_q at each |q|=1: compute Im φ_q(w)=(1−|w|²)/|q+w|² and the explicit inverse ψ(u)=q(i−u)/(i+u), then check continuity by an ε-δ estimate.

items.title: Pure configuration braid group
items.statement: For a fixed ordered q of n distinct points in int D², PB_n=π₁(F_n(D²),q); the radial equivalence also identifies this with the corresponding group for int D². This is a configuration-space definition, before the geometric-braid comparison.

references.title: Juan González-Meneses, Basic results on braid groups, §§1.1–1.3 and 2.1, printed pp. 3–6, 11–13

items.proof_strategy: Use based loops and the explicit closed/interior disk equivalence, including the radial basepoint path. The choice of q is fixed throughout the exact sequence.

items.title: Unordered configuration braid group
items.statement: For the same q, B_n^conf=π₁(C_n(D²),[q]); retain the superscript conf until the later geometric identification, and use the corresponding int D² model through radial equivalence.

references.title: Juan González-Meneses, Basic results on braid groups, §§1.1–1.3 and 2.1, printed pp. 3–6, 11–13

items.proof_strategy: Use the orbit basepoint and fundamental-group multiplication inherited from published based loops. Do not identify this group with the abstract Artin presentation at this stage.

items.title: Endpoint monodromy of a configuration loop
items.statement: For an unordered based loop α, lift from q and let e_α(j) be the endpoint position occupied by label j. Define π([α])=e_α^{-1}∈S_n. With the published first-then-second loop product and ordinary function composition, π:B_n^conf→S_n is a homomorphism.

references.title: Juan González-Meneses, Basic results on braid groups, §§1.1–1.3 and 2.1, printed pp. 3–6, 11–13

items.proof_strategy: Covering path lifting and homotopy lifting make e_α depend only on [α]. The published covering monodromy is a right action: e_{αβ}=e_β∘e_α. Inverting gives π(αβ)=π(α)∘π(β). This fixes the convention needed by later Artin and geometric comparisons.

items.title: Configuration braid short exact sequence
items.statement: For every n≥0, 1→PB_n→B_n^conf→S_n→1 is exact, where the first arrow is induced by F_n(D²)→C_n(D²) and the last is inverse endpoint monodromy.

references.title: Juan González-Meneses, Basic results on braid groups, §§1.1–1.3 and 2.1, printed pp. 3–6, 11–13
Fadell–Neuwirth, Configuration Spaces, §II Theorems 1 and 3, printed pp. 111–114

items.proof_strategy: Connected covering theory makes the first map injective. A loop has trivial endpoint permutation exactly when its lift from q closes, which identifies its kernel with the image. For each adjacent pair of standard points, rotate that pair by a half turn in a small disk avoiding all others; the resulting unordered loop has the adjacent transposition as π-image. Adjacent transpositions generate S_n; n=0,1 are trivial. The inverse endpoint convention does not change an individual transposition.

items.title: Local triviality of forgetting configuration points
items.statement: For a Hausdorff boundaryless locally Euclidean d-manifold M with d≥2 and m,n≥1, forgetting the last n points F_{m+n}(M)→F_m(M) is locally trivial over each base configuration, with fiber F_n(M minus its m retained points).

references.title: Fadell–Neuwirth, Configuration Spaces, §II Theorems 1 and 3, printed pp. 111–114
Juan González-Meneses, Basic results on braid groups, §§1.1–1.3 and 2.1, printed pp. 3–6, 11–13

items.proof_strategy: Around retained points a_j choose disjoint Euclidean balls with smaller concentric balls. For nearby x_j move a_j to x_j by a radial bump homeomorphism supported in its ball; in coordinates use y↦y+(1−|y−a_j|/r)(x_j−a_j) for |y−a_j|≤r and identity outside, with |x_j−a_j|<r. The bump b(y)=max(0,1−|y−a_j|/r) is 1/r-Lipschitz; when |x_j−a_j|<r, y↦y+b(y)(x_j−a_j) is bi-Lipschitz onto its image. For any target z, the inverse equation y=z−b(y)(x_j−a_j) is a contraction of the complete coordinate space with constant |x_j−a_j|/r<1, proving surjectivity and a jointly continuous inverse on a smaller parameter neighborhood. The map fixes the ball boundary and all points outside it. Compose the finitely many disjoint movers H_x. Trivialize by (x,y)↦(x,H_x^{-1}(y)) on forgotten points; inverse uses H_x. No global metric or paracompactness is assumed.

items.title: Fadell–Neuwirth forgetful bundle and disk fibration
items.statement: For a nonempty connected boundaryless d-manifold M, d≥2, and m,n≥1, F_{m+n}(M)→F_m(M) is a locally trivial bundle with fiber F_n(M∖{m retained points}). For M=int D², assuming AC, this bundle is numerable and is a Hurewicz fibration.

references.title: Fadell–Neuwirth, Configuration Spaces, §II Theorems 1 and 3, printed pp. 111–114
Juan González-Meneses, Basic results on braid groups, §§1.1–1.3 and 2.1, printed pp. 3–6, 11–13
Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, §4.2, printed pp. 379–380

items.proof_strategy: Apply the local mover lemma for arbitrary M; no global paracompactness is claimed. In the disk case F_m(int D²) is a metric open subset of R^{2m}. Invoke AC to select a chart for each member of a subordinate refinement and to well-order the lifting construction; AC implies DC by choosing one successor for each nonempty successor set. The published metric partition-of-unity corollary explicitly uses AC and DC. Its partition makes the displayed local-triviality cover numerable. Apply the published numerable-bundle Hurewicz theorem. This choice assumption applies only to the Hurewicz upgrade.

title: Ordered and Unordered Configuration Spaces — Examples

items.title: Two ordered points in the plane
items.statement: F₂(C)≅C×C* by (z₁,z₂)↦((z₁+z₂)/2,z₂−z₁).

references.title: Juan González-Meneses, Basic results on braid groups, §§1.1–1.3 and 2.1, printed pp. 3–6, 11–13

items.proof_strategy: The inverse sends (c,w) to (c−w/2,c+w/2). Both maps are continuous and w≠0 is exactly the collision-free condition.

items.title: The two-point quotient cover
items.statement: Under the preceding coordinates, the transposition acts by (c,w)↦(c,−w); C₂(C)≅C×(C*/{±1}), and a half rotation of w has nontrivial endpoint monodromy.

references.title: Juan González-Meneses, Basic results on braid groups, §§1.1–1.3 and 2.1, printed pp. 3–6, 11–13

items.proof_strategy: Use the ordered-coordinate homeomorphism, let w(t)=w₀e^{πit}, and observe [w(1)]=[w(0)] while the lifted endpoint is −w₀. The transposition is its own inverse, so the convention for π agrees. The orbit quotient has two sheets locally.

items.title: Collisions destroy freeness
items.statement: For n≥2 and any nonempty X, the action of S_n on X^n is not free when two coordinates coincide.

references.title: Juan González-Meneses, Basic results on braid groups, §§1.1–1.3 and 2.1, printed pp. 3–6, 11–13

items.proof_strategy: Choose an x∈X and a tuple with its first two entries equal to x. Their transposition is nonidentity yet fixes the tuple. This contrasts with the collision-free action.

items.title: The natural two-point quotient is not injective
items.statement: For distinct z₁,z₂, (z₁,z₂) and (z₂,z₁) are distinct elements of F₂(C) with the same image in C₂(C), so the natural quotient map is not a homeomorphism.

references.title: Juan González-Meneses, Basic results on braid groups, §§1.1–1.3 and 2.1, printed pp. 3–6, 11–13

items.proof_strategy: The two tuples differ since z₁≠z₂ and lie in one S₂ orbit. The claim concerns this quotient map only; it does not assert nonhomeomorphism of the total spaces.

title: Graded Quiver Algebras and Derived Tensor Functors

items.title: Integral path ring of a finite quiver
items.statement: For a finite quiver Q, ZQ is the free abelian group on directed finite paths, including length-zero vertex idempotents. Multiply composable paths by left-to-right concatenation and noncomposable paths by zero; 1 is the finite sum of vertex paths.

references.title: Khovanov–Seidel, Quivers, Floer cohomology, and braid group actions, §§1b and 2a–2d, printed pp. 3–4 and 9–14

items.proof_strategy: Check associativity on basis paths and distributivity by bilinear extension. State the left-to-right convention so A e_i consists of paths ending at i and e_i A consists of paths beginning at i.

items.title: Khovanov–Seidel type A algebra
items.statement: For m≥1 let A_m be the quotient of ZQ for the doubled line 0↔1↔⋯↔m by (i−1|i|i+1)=(i+1|i|i−1)=0, (i|i+1|i)=(i|i−1|i) for 0<i<m, and (0|1|0)=0. Vertices and arrows (i|i+1) have internal degree 0; arrows (i+1|i) have degree 1.

references.title: Khovanov–Seidel, Quivers, Floer cohomology, and braid group actions, §§1b and 2a–2d, printed pp. 3–4 and 9–14

items.proof_strategy: The relations are homogeneous of internal degree 1 for returns and of their path degree for monotone paths, so the quotient has the claimed Z-grading. Respect the source left-to-right path convention and endpoint omission.

items.title: The 4m+1 path basis
items.statement: As a graded abelian group A_m is free of rank 4m+1 on its m+1 vertices, 2m arrows, and one degree-one length-two return at each vertex i=1,…,m; all longer paths vanish.

references.title: Khovanov–Seidel, Quivers, Floer cohomology, and braid group actions, §§1b and 2a–2d, printed pp. 3–4 and 9–14

items.proof_strategy: Work in path length, separate from internal degree. Monotone subpaths of length two vanish; every alternating length-three path is equivalent, using the interior-return equality, to a path containing a forbidden monotone subpath or the zero return at vertex 0. Check the endpoint m case explicitly. Thus length≥3 vanishes. In length two, the only surviving classes are one return at each i>0, while the 0 return is zero. Since the relation ideal is generated by homogeneous length-two relations, multiplication by positive-length paths cannot create new relations in lengths zero, one, or two. These classes are independent, giving (m+1)+2m+m=4m+1.

items.title: Graded A_m-modules and vertex projectives
items.statement: A_m-mod consists of finitely generated Z-graded left A_m-modules and degree-zero maps. This finite-module category is abelian. Internal shift is M{r}_d=M_{d−r}. Put P_i=A_m e_i and _iP=e_i A_m; each is a finite graded projective on its indicated side.

references.title: Khovanov–Seidel, Quivers, Floer cohomology, and braid group actions, §§1b and 2a–2d, printed pp. 3–4 and 9–14

items.proof_strategy: Since A_m is finite free as a Z-module by the path basis and Z is Noetherian, the published finite-module theorem makes its underlying Z-module Noetherian. Every left ideal is a Z-submodule, hence finitely generated over Z and by the same elements as a left ideal. Thus A_m is left Noetherian; finite generated graded modules and their graded kernels, images and cokernels stay finite generated, so this category is abelian. The finite idempotent decomposition A_m=⊕P_i and its right analogue exhibit P_i and _iP as finite shifted-free summands; apply the graded-projective supplier separately on both sides. Distinguish the paper notation A_m(i) from the inherited shift braces.

items.title: Vertex modules and prime quotients
items.statement: For each i=0,…,m, S_i is Z in internal degree zero, with e_i acting as identity and every other positive-length path and vertex idempotent acting by zero. For a prime p, S_i/pS_i is the corresponding Z/p vertex module; under M{r}_d=M_{d-r}, S_i{r} is concentrated in degree r.

references.title: Khovanov–Seidel, Quivers, Floer cohomology, and braid group actions, §§1b and 2a–2d, printed pp. 3–4 and 9–14

items.proof_strategy: Check that arrows and all relations act trivially, so the displayed action descends from A_m. The sequence 0→S_i --p→ S_i→S_i/pS_i→0 is degreewise exact for each prime p.

items.title: Finite resolutions of the vertex modules
items.statement: For each i the vertex module S_i has a finite graded projective resolution obtained by signed totalization of the Khovanov–Seidel grid of shifted P_j; each S_i/pS_i also has a finite graded projective resolution.

references.title: Khovanov–Seidel, Quivers, Floer cohomology, and braid group actions, §§1b and 2a–2d, printed pp. 3–4 and 9–14
Charles Weibel, Introduction to Homological Algebra, ch. 2 §2.2, pp. 36–38

items.proof_strategy: Use the finite grid displayed in KS Proposition 2.1, with horizontal and vertical maps right multiplication by adjacent arrows and internal shifts chosen to make every map degree zero. The two zero monotone-path relations give d_h²=d_v²=0; equality of the two return paths gives commuting squares. Insert sign (−1)^{horizontal degree} in the vertical differential. Verify each column directly on the four path-basis types: the image of each incoming arrow map equals the kernel of the outgoing map except at its top entry. Filter the total complex by columns; its first spectral sequence therefore has only the top-row homology, whose horizontal complex is the augmentation to S_i and is exact by the same path-basis kernel/image calculation. Finiteness makes totalization and convergence elementary. Apply the degree-zero short exact sequence 0→S_i --p→S_i→S_i/pS_i→0 and the explicit mapping cone of multiplication by p on that finite projective resolution to get the p-quotient resolution; the cone maps onto S_i/pS_i with the expected homology because multiplication by p is injective on S_i. The word “simple” in the inherited ID does not assert that Z-valued S_i is a simple A_m-module.

items.title: Finite graded projective resolutions are extension stable
items.statement: In the abelian category of graded A_m-modules, if 0→M′→M→M″→0 is degreewise exact and M′,M″ have finite resolutions by finitely generated graded projectives, then M has such a resolution, of length at most max(pd M′,pd M″).

references.title: Charles Weibel, Introduction to Homological Algebra, ch. 2 §2.2, pp. 36–38
Khovanov–Seidel, Quivers, Floer cohomology, and braid group actions, §§1b and 2a–2d, printed pp. 3–4 and 9–14

items.proof_strategy: Construct the graded horseshoe degreewise. Given the two finite free/projective resolutions, lift the projective term over M″ through M and add the M′ term; the kernel fits a degreewise short exact sequence. Iterate, with differential signs chosen so squares commute. The middle term at each degree is the finite direct sum of the two projectives and vanishes above the maximum bound. Every lift is chosen from a finite generating family; no countable-choice hypothesis is used. Use the actual module category rather than relying on the published arbitrary-abelian-category element chase.

items.title: Finite homological dimension of A_m
items.statement: Every finitely generated graded A_m-module has a finite resolution by finitely generated graded projectives; the lengths are bounded in terms of m, so the finite graded module category has finite homological dimension.

references.title: Khovanov–Seidel, Quivers, Floer cohomology, and braid group actions, §§1b and 2a–2d, printed pp. 3–4 and 9–14
Charles Weibel, Introduction to Homological Algebra, ch. 2 §2.2, pp. 36–38

items.proof_strategy: The path basis makes A_m finite free over Z and its positive-length arrow ideal J nilpotent with J³=0. Filter M by J^kM, k=0,1,2,3. Each quotient is a finitely generated graded module over A_m/J≈Z^{m+1}, with finite degree support. Apply the published PID structure theorem to each vertex/degree component; split free and prime-power cyclic summands, then filter prime powers to shifts of S_i and S_i/pS_i. Use their finite resolutions and the finite graded extension lemma along this finite filtration. The uniform bound is max_i pd(S_i)+1, independent of M; no arbitrary-length composition-series assumption over Z is made.

items.title: Bounded finite projective model for Khovanov-Seidel modules
items.statement: For m≥1, the canonical functor K^b(proj^gr A_m)→D^b(A_m-mod) is an exact equivalence.
items.strategy: The path basis makes A_m a finite Z-module, hence left Noetherian: every left ideal is a finite Z-submodule. The category of finitely generated graded modules is abelian and has enough finite graded projectives via homogeneous free presentations. Khovanov-Seidel Proposition 2.1, supplied locally by the finite-homological-dimension theorem, gives each finite module a finite projective resolution. For a bounded complex C, induct on its number of nonzero terms. Its upper brutal subcomplex sigma_{>a}C and bottom-degree quotient C^a[-a] each have bounded finite-projective models, where a is the lowest nonzero cohomological degree. In the distinguished triangle sigma_{>a}C→C→C^a[-a]→(sigma_{>a}C)[1], represent the connecting morphism between those models by a chain map: bounded projective complexes are K-projective by a finite descending null-homotopy lift, so their derived Hom needs no roof. The shifted cone of that map is a bounded finite-projective model of C; a morphism of triangles compares it to C. The same finite K-projective argument proves full faithfulness of K^b(proj^gr A_m) in D^b(A_m-mod), and shifts/cones prove exactness. The construction uses finite choices only; it does not invoke the unbuilt general HA-21 result or an unbounded replacement.

references.title: Khovanov and Seidel, Quivers, Floer cohomology, and braid group actions, sections 2a-2d
Charles Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, chapter 10 section 10.4

items.title: Bounded projective homotopy category
items.statement: Let C_m=K^b(proj^gr A_m) with homological shift [1] distinct from internal shift {1}. Under finite-projective bounded-comparison hypotheses, C_m identifies with D^b(A_m-mod), the bounded derived category of finitely generated graded A_m-modules.

references.title: Khovanov–Seidel, Quivers, Floer cohomology, and braid group actions, §§1b and 2a–2d, printed pp. 3–4 and 9–14
Charles Weibel, Introduction to Homological Algebra, ch. 10 §10.4, pp. 387–390

items.proof_strategy: Use the finite rank path basis to establish that A_m is left Noetherian, so finitely generated graded modules form an abelian category. The preceding finite-homological-dimension theorem supplies a uniform projective bound. Apply the local bounded finite-projective model lemma: finite resolutions, upper brutal subcomplexes, degreewise split extension triangles, and finite projective lifts give K^b(proj^gr A_m) equivalent to D^b(A_m-mod). Keep [1] and {1} distinct.
items.strategy: Define C_m=K^b(proj^gr A_m) with homological [1] and internal {1}. The preceding local lemma proves the exact equivalence to D^b(A_m-mod) using A_m-specific Noetherianity and finite homological dimension. The notation and two distinct shifts follow Khovanov-Seidel section 2c; do not invoke unbuilt generic perfect-complex pages.

items.title: Two-sided projective U_i tensor functors
items.statement: For 1≤i≤m put U_i=P_i⊗_Z _iP, an A_m–A_m graded bimodule, and let U_i(M)=U_i⊗_{A_m}M. U_i is finite graded projective on both sides, so the functor is exact and preserves finite graded projectives.

references.title: Khovanov–Seidel, Quivers, Floer cohomology, and braid group actions, §§1b and 2a–2d, printed pp. 3–4 and 9–14

items.proof_strategy: Use the 4m+1 path basis to see _iP and P_i are finite free Z-modules. As a left module, U_i is a finite direct sum of internal shifts of P_i; as a right module it is a finite sum of shifts of _iP. Apply the two independent clauses of the HA-18 tensor theorem: right projectivity gives flatness/exactness, left projectivity gives preservation of projectives. Do not infer the second clause from right projectivity alone.

items.title: Temperley–Lieb relations for U_i
items.statement: For 1≤i≤m, U_i²≅U_i⊕U_i{1}; for adjacent valid indices, U_iU_{i±1}U_i≅U_i{1}; and U_iU_j=0 if |i−j|>1, as natural graded functors.

references.title: Khovanov–Seidel, Quivers, Floer cohomology, and braid group actions, §§1b and 2a–2d, printed pp. 3–4 and 9–14

items.proof_strategy: Use graded balanced associativity to reduce every composite to P_i⊗_Z(e_iA_me_j)⊗_Z _jP. From the path basis, e_iA_me_i has basis e_i and the degree-one return for i>0; e_iA_me_{i±1} is a single arrow, whose degree is 0 or 1. In a triple adjacent composite the two arrows have total degree 1, regardless of direction. Distant corners vanish. Exhibit basis-preserving bimodule isomorphisms and apply tensor to each module; check the right/left corner convention and endpoints.

items.title: Khovanov–Seidel beta and gamma maps
items.statement: β_i:U_i→A_m is multiplication. γ_i:A_m→U_i{−1} is the degree-zero bimodule map determined by γ_i(1)=(i−1|i)⊗(i|i−1)+(i+1|i)⊗(i|i+1)+(i)⊗(i|i−1|i)+(i|i−1|i)⊗(i), with the i+1 term omitted for i=m. For i=1 the return paths use the equal interior representatives.

references.title: Khovanov–Seidel, Quivers, Floer cohomology, and braid group actions, §§1b and 2a–2d, printed pp. 3–4 and 9–14

items.proof_strategy: Read KS equations (2.6)–(2.7) in its left-to-right path convention. Verify γ_i(1) has internal degree one before shift {−1}; check aγ_i(1)=γ_i(1)a on each vertex idempotent and arrow. Each equality reduces to the zero monotone paths, equal interior returns and zero loop at 0. This centrality makes the unit-image formula a bimodule map. Multiplication is bilinear and degree zero. Check the endpoint omissions separately.

items.title: Signed totalization of graded A_m bimodule actions
items.statement: For a bounded complex R^• of graded A_m-A_m bimodules and a bounded complex X^• of graded left A_m-modules, define (R⊗_{A_m}X)^n=⊕_{p+q=n}R^p⊗_{A_m}X^q, with d(r⊗x)=d_Rr⊗x+(-1)^p r⊗d_Xx for r∈R^p; internal degrees add independently of homological degrees.
items.strategy: Translate the published chain-complex tensor totalization to cochain grading. Balanced tensor and the graded shift supplier define each summand. The two cross terms of d² cancel because d_R and d_X commute on pure tensors and their Koszul signs differ by one; d_R²=d_X²=0. Boundedness makes each diagonal a finite direct sum. A homotopy h on X tensors with the identity on R using sign (-1)^p on R^p⊗h, giving a homotopy of total complexes; the analogous construction works on R. This is the bounded bimodule action of KS section 2c, with the cochain sign verified directly and tied to the published tensor-total-complex definition.

references.title: Khovanov and Seidel, Quivers, Floer cohomology, and braid group actions, sections 2a-2d

items.title: Bounded two-sided projective bimodule complexes act on C_m
items.statement: A bounded complex R^• of graded A_m-A_m bimodules whose terms are finitely generated graded projective on both sides gives an exact triangulated functor R^•⊗_{A_m}- on C_m=K^b(proj^gr A_m); under C_m≃D^b(A_m-mod), it is the derived tensor functor.
items.strategy: For X^q a finite graded projective left module, X^q is a retract of a finite shifted free module. Then R^p⊗_{A_m}X^q is a retract of a finite sum of internal shifts of R^p, hence finite graded projective on the left. The signed finite-diagonal totalization therefore stays in C_m. The explicit tensor-homotopy sign from the preceding definition makes the functor descend to homotopy classes; a direct signed identification R⊗Cone(f)≅Cone(R⊗f) shows it preserves distinguished triangles. Right projectivity makes each R^p flat, and a bounded complex of right-flat terms preserves quasi-isomorphisms between bounded complexes by the published flat-tensor lemma. Consequently its C_m action agrees, through the bounded projective equivalence, with left derived tensor. Left and right projectivity are used for different obligations, exactly as in KS section 2c.

references.title: Khovanov and Seidel, Quivers, Floer cohomology, and braid group actions, sections 2a-2d
Charles Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, chapter 10 section 10.4

items.title: Positive and negative twist complexes
items.statement: Set R_i=[U_i --β_i→A_m] with A_m in homological degree 0, and R_i^{-1}=[A_m --γ_i→U_i{−1}] with A_m in degree 0. These bounded two-sided-projective bimodule complexes define derived tensor functors on the specified bounded finite-module category.

references.title: Khovanov–Seidel, Quivers, Floer cohomology, and braid group actions, §§1b and 2a–2d, printed pp. 3–4 and 9–14
Charles Weibel, Introduction to Homological Algebra, ch. 10 §10.4, pp. 387–390

items.proof_strategy: The maps are degree-zero bimodule maps, so they form the displayed two-term complexes with A_m in degree zero. Check each term is finite projective on both sides using U_i and the regular bimodule. The local signed totalization and bounded two-sided-projective action lemma give exact tensor actions on C_m and identify them with derived tensor through the local bounded finite-projective model. Check left and right projectivity separately and use the source's negative-twist cone sign.
items.strategy: Use the beta and gamma bimodule maps to form the indicated two-term complexes with A_m in homological degree zero. The path-basis calculation makes A_m and U_i finite graded projective on both left and right; the local signed totalization and two-sided-projective action lemma therefore define exact functors on C_m and identify them with derived tensor on D^b(A_m-mod). Check gamma has internal degree zero after the {-1} shift. This defines the complexes and their actions; inverse and braid-relation claims remain for BG-15.

items.title: Triangulated K-zero of the Khovanov-Seidel projective category
items.statement: Let K_0(C_m) be the abelian group on isomorphism classes [X] of objects of C_m=K^b(proj^gr A_m), modulo [Y]=[X]+[Z] for every distinguished triangle X→Y→Z→X[1]. Use an essentially small skeleton of C_m to form the free abelian group.
items.strategy: The bounded projective homotopy category is triangulated because cones and homological shifts of bounded finite-projective complexes remain bounded finite-projective. A_m is a fixed finite Z-algebra, so finite graded modules, finite projectives, and their bounded complexes have only a set of isomorphism classes; a skeleton exists. Apply Stacks Definition 13.28.1 to that skeleton. This local definition is sufficient for the shift comparison and does not import the unbuilt general HA-21 pair.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Derived Categories, section 28, K-groups (tag 0FCM)
Khovanov and Seidel, Quivers, Floer cohomology, and braid group actions, sections 2a-2d

items.title: Homological and internal shifts on Khovanov-Seidel K-zero
items.statement: In K_0(C_m), [X[1]]=-[X]. The exact internal shift {1} acts by an invertible operator q, so [X{r}]=q^r[X] and K_0(C_m) is a Z[q,q^{-1}]-module.
items.strategy: Stacks Definition 13.28.1 uses the distinguished triangle X→0→X[1]→X[1], whose relation gives 0=[X]+[X[1]]. The internal shift is exact: applying it termwise commutes with homological shifts and mapping cones, hence preserves triangle relations and induces an automorphism of K_0; its inverse is {-1}. Define q by this automorphism and iterate for r∈Z. This proves the specific K-zero statement needed by the B counterexample without a graded Cartan pairing.

references.title: The Stacks Project, Derived Categories, section 28, K-groups (tag 0FCM)
Khovanov and Seidel, Quivers, Floer cohomology, and braid group actions, sections 2a-2d

title: Graded Quiver Algebras and Derived Tensor Functors — Examples

items.title: A₂ algebra and vertex projectives
items.statement: For m=2, A₂ has nine basis paths: e₀,e₁,e₂, four adjacent arrows, and the degree-one return loops at vertices 1 and 2. P₀,P₁,P₂ are spanned respectively by paths ending at 0,1,2.

references.title: Khovanov–Seidel, Quivers, Floer cohomology, and braid group actions, §§1b and 2a–2d, printed pp. 3–4 and 9–14

items.proof_strategy: List P₀={e₀,(1|0)}, P₁={e₁,(0|1),(2|1),(1|0|1)}, and P₂={e₂,(1|2),(2|1|2)} with inherited degrees. Multiply paths by concatenation; every monotone length-two and length-three product vanishes, (1|0|1)=(1|2|1), and the 0 return vanishes. These rules determine the full multiplication table.

items.title: A₂ vertex-module resolution
items.statement: For A₂ the vertex module S₂ has an explicit graded projective resolution 0→P₀→P₁→P₂→S₂→0, where both projective maps are right multiplication by the degree-zero arrows (0|1) and (1|2).

references.title: Khovanov–Seidel, Quivers, Floer cohomology, and braid group actions, §§1b and 2a–2d, printed pp. 3–4 and 9–14

items.proof_strategy: Check the composite is the zero monotone path (0|1|2). P₂→S₂ kills the arrow (1|2) and return loop; these span the image of P₁→P₂. The kernel of P₁→P₂ is spanned by (0|1) and (1|0|1), exactly the image of P₀→P₁; the first map is injective on its two basis paths. Thus every term and differential is explicit and degree zero.

items.title: Signed total differential of a twist action
items.statement: For a two-term projective complex X and R_i=[U_i→A_m], R_i⊗_{A_m}X has total differential d(r⊗x)=d_Rr⊗x+(−1)^{deg_h r}r⊗d_Xx, with four terms on the two-column double complex.

references.title: Khovanov–Seidel, Quivers, Floer cohomology, and braid group actions, §§1b and 2a–2d, printed pp. 3–4 and 9–14
Charles Weibel, Introduction to Homological Algebra, ch. 10 §10.4, pp. 387–390

items.proof_strategy: Place U_i in homological degree −1 and A_m in degree 0, and X in two consecutive degrees. Write all four direct-summand terms and their horizontal and vertical maps; verify mixed terms cancel because the maps are chain maps and the sign uses homological, never internal, degree. The graded bimodule tensor is balanced and β is degree zero.
items.strategy: For a two-term projective X and R_i=[U_i→A_m], list the four tensor summands in the two-column double complex and use d(r⊗x)=d_Rr⊗x+(-1)^p r⊗d_Xx for r in homological degree p. Show the two mixed differential terms cancel and the internal degree is unaffected by the homological sign. The local signed-totalization definition supplies this rule.

items.title: Internal and homological shifts differ
items.statement: On the bounded graded projective category, internal shift {1} and homological shift [1] are not naturally isomorphic: the first shifts internal grading while leaving homological placement fixed, and the second changes homological parity and sends [X] to −[X] in triangulated K₀.

references.title: Khovanov–Seidel, Quivers, Floer cohomology, and braid group actions, §§1b and 2a–2d, printed pp. 3–4 and 9–14
Charles Weibel, Introduction to Homological Algebra, ch. 10 §10.4, pp. 387–390

items.proof_strategy: Take a nonzero projective P_i concentrated in homological degree zero. The Hom group from P_i{1} to P_i[1] in K^b is zero, while the identity of P_i{1} is nonzero, so the shifts are not naturally isomorphic. Use the local triangulated K_0 definition and shift lemma to state [X[1]]=-[X] and [X{1}]=q[X] without claiming nontriviality of negation on every K_0 class.
items.strategy: Take the nonzero projective P_i concentrated in homological degree zero. P_i{1} still has its only nonzero homology in degree zero, whereas P_i[1] has it in degree -1; hence these objects cannot be isomorphic in C_m or D^b, so the two shift functors are not naturally isomorphic. In local triangulated K_0, the cone triangle gives [X[1]]=-[X], while the exact internal shift acts by q. This retains both the homological-support witness and the intended K-zero comparison.
